simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Simplicity's read is correct on close inspection. The `--include-backlog` flag was AI-introduced in interview Round 4 (line 57 of `005-scope-change-skill-interview.md`) as part of the recommended answer, and the user confirmed without naming a use case where they would actually flip the flag. Confirming an AI-recommended option is NOT the same as the user surfacing a second consumer with a stated need — the Simplicity sub-clause's evidence threshold ('Do not introduce config knobs without a concrete second consumer demanding them') is not met. The user's explicit framing in Round 4 was 'Backlog excluded by default to avoid surfacing every queued task' — that's the design choice; the flag is the speculative escape hatch. Compare to 002-develop-skill's split outcome on simplicity-r1-f1 where R6's cap had a documented user edit (interview line 78) naming two use cases — that's the higher bar, and `--include-backlog` doesn't clear it. Going with the Simplicity proposal: drop the flag from R8 and AC-8.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: R8 revised to drop `--include-backlog` clause: 'Linear (when MCP available) — every issue where `feature == {NNN-slug}` AND `status` ∈ {`In Progress`, `In Review`} AND the issue's Anchor R-ID is in the changed-R-ID set. Backlog tickets are excluded; v1 ships with this hard-coded.' AC-8 simplified to drop the conditional second clause about `--include-backlog`. Consumers who later report friction can request the flag as a v2 enhancement when a concrete use case surfaces.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill creep is real and matches the precedent set by 002-develop-skill's surgical-r1-f1 (where `specflow:misc --auto`'s payload schema was implicitly extended). R10.1 assumes `specflow:decision` accepts arbitrary keyed-blocks within `references` AND an `id_prefix` parameter; neither is documented in the current Phase 3 schema. Option (b) (explicit dependency call-out) preserves the structured-fields information value (which `/insights` Phase 3 cross-feature filterability depends on) while making the cross-skill dependency loud. Going with option (b).
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: R10.1 sharpened to add explicit schema dependency: 'Schema dependency: R10.1 depends on `specflow:decision` accepting an arbitrary keyed-block within `references` AND accepting an `id_prefix: "SC"` parameter on invocation. If the current Phase 3 `specflow:decision` schema (per `skills/decision/SKILL.md`) does not accept these, ship them via a `specflow:decision` enhancement PRD before `specflow:scope-change` v1 lands.' AC-10 mirrors the same dependency clause. The cross-skill dependency is now named, not buried in implementation.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: Unstated load-bearing assumption is real. R4's `~~text~~` strikethrough markup was specified as a human-readable diff signal in interview Round 2 (line 44), but R5's surgical-PRD-synthesis step and R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines` reference list both treat the markup as a parseable contract without naming it as such. Line-number references (`round-2.line-78`) drift if the strikethrough adds characters mid-line — that's a real failure mode. Going with the proposed sharpen: name strikethrough markup as the canonical machine-readable signal in R4, and change R10.1's reference shape from line-numbers to round+anchor-text (drift-resistant because the wrapped characters are byte-stable).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R4 extended with the parser-contract clause: 'The `~~text~~` strikethrough markup paired with the `(superseded by Scope change {YYYY-MM-DD})` parenthetical IS the canonical machine-readable signal for supersession. `specflow:prd` Phase C synthesis (R5) parses Resolved lines for `~~...~~` runs paired with the supersession note to compute the changed-R-ID set; `specflow:decision` invocation (R10.1) uses the same parse to build the `superseded_resolved_lines` reference. The parenthetical date is the supersession-event anchor.' R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines` shape changed from line-number to round+anchor-text: `superseded_resolved_lines: [{round: 2, anchor: "foo flag defaults to true"}, ...]`. AC-4 extended to verify markup-as-contract: every `~~...~~` run must have a matching `(superseded by Scope change {YYYY-MM-DD})` note within the same line; orphan strikethrough runs are a failed step (i).

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Non-binary AC at the across-source boundary is real. The lens question fails on draft PRs (gh `--state open` includes drafts; AC-8 doesn't say whether to keep them) and Linear custom intermediate statuses (the canonical In Progress / In Review enumeration silently excludes Blocked / On Hold without naming it). Both are concrete failure modes a fresh agent compiling the impact list would hit. Going with the proposed sharpen: include draft PRs by default with `(draft)` annotation, exclude Linear custom statuses with a chat-line note surfacing the count.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: AC-8 extended with the boundary clauses: '(a) Open PRs: `gh pr list --state open` includes draft PRs; v1 INCLUDES draft PRs in the impact list with a `(draft)` annotation per entry so the user can triage accordingly. (b) Linear: only the literal canonical statuses `In Progress` and `In Review` count by default; project-defined custom intermediate statuses (Blocked, On Hold, etc.) are NOT auto-included — a chat-line note at impact-list compilation surfaces `(Linear: N tickets in custom statuses {list} not auto-included; review manually if relevant)`.' R8 updated to reference the explicit boundary, not the implicit canonical-statuses-only enumeration.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: Disagreeing with the orphan-AC framing. R12 reads: 'Every sub-skill invocation runs in a forked sub-agent context per `templates/orchestrator-pattern.md`. Verbatim file content is injected via command substitution; intermediate artefacts land in `admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-scope-change/`; only file paths return to the parent context.' The `templates/orchestrator-pattern.md` reference IS the canonical location of the token-budget targets — R12 binds the skill to that template's contract by reference. The 25K parent-context number in AC-13 is named as 'tighter than `specflow:develop`'s 30K because scope-change has fewer sub-skill steps' — that's a scope-change-specific calibration of the template's general target, not a fresh contract. Compare to 002-develop-skill's goal-r1-f1 (PRD-anchor format) which DID need a new R because the format was not in any referenced template; here the bounds are derived from a template R12 already cites. Adding R13 would be redundant — orchestrator-pattern.md plus R12's binding-by-reference plus AC-13's scope-change-specific calibration is the surgical shape. The orphan-AC heuristic is correct in general but mis-fires here because the binding-by-reference IS the R-level expression. Push back: keep R12 + AC-13 as written; do NOT add R13.
goal-r1-f2.revision_applied: No revision applied to R12 or AC-13. AC-13's `Verifies` line clarified to make the binding-by-reference explicit: '(Verifies R12 — orchestrator-pattern compliance, which binds to `templates/orchestrator-pattern.md`'s token-budget targets; the 25K/2K numbers are scope-change-specific calibrations of those targets, derived from the eight-step flow vs `specflow:develop`'s longer flow.)' The minor clarification in AC-13's parenthetical preserves the surgical shape without creating R13.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill state contamination is real. The R2 trigger (a) (Verifier rejection option 3) fires from inside a paused `specflow:develop` run, and the lifecycle-handoff contract was not specified in either skill's PRD. The circular-reference risk in the impact list (the rejected task surfacing as its own trigger) is a concrete bug that R8 + R7.1 would silently produce. Phase 2 `specflow:develop` Phase F.3 says 'abort' but the cleanup-and-handoff is silent. Going with the proposed extensions: state-handoff clause on R2, self-reference exclusion clause on R8.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: R2 extended with the state-handoff clause: 'When trigger (a) (Verifier rejection option 3) fires, `specflow:develop` exits cleanly before the y/n prompt — the in-flight task's `task-history.json.status` is updated to `aborted_for_scope_change` (a new status value distinct from `in_progress` so R7.1 partial-completion handling does NOT misclassify the aborted task as in-flight). The `specflow:develop` scratch directory is preserved (not cleaned) so the user can resume after scope-change closes. After scope-change step (viii) cleanup, the user re-invokes `specflow:develop {NNN-slug}` manually — there is NO auto-resume from scope-change back to develop (auto-resume crosses the user-always-elects line).' R8 extended with self-reference exclusion: 'The impact-list source-section enumeration EXCLUDES the task that triggered the scope-change invocation when scope-change fires via R2 trigger (a). The exclusion is recorded as a single line in the `## task-history.json` section: `(triggering task T-{N} excluded from impact list — its abort is the precondition for this scope-change run)`.' AC-2 and AC-8 sub-clauses added to verify both contracts. Note: the new `aborted_for_scope_change` status value introduces a `task-history.json` schema dependency on `specflow:develop` accepting the new value; surfaced in R2 with the same explicit-dependency framing surgical-r1-f1 used for R10.1.
